false_positives.issue: trim_docstring computes the minimum indentation over all non-blank lines, including the first line. For the common docstring form with a summary immediately after the opening quotes and indented body lines below it, the first line has zero indent, so indent becomes 0 and the body lines keep their leading spaces. inspect.cleandoc computes the margin from lines[1:] only, so this changes the parsed reST body (indented text becomes a block quote).
false_positives.suggestion: indent = min((len(line) - len(line.lstrip()) for line in lines[1:] if line.lstrip()), default=0)

false_positives.issue: line[indent:].rstrip() strips trailing spaces from every continuation line, whereas inspect.cleandoc preserves them. reST hard line breaks (two trailing spaces at the end of a line) are therefore lost when rendering docstrings.
false_positives.suggestion: Use line[indent:] without rstrip, and trim only leading/trailing blank lines instead of stripping whitespace from content lines.

The new loop processes only rows = min(m, n) rows from the bottom. When n < m, nonzero rows above the bottom n rows are never considered, so matrices whose pivot rows lie above that range no longer get their HNF computed. For example, a 3x1 matrix with only the top row nonzero is reduced to a 3x0 result, whereas the old loop continued upward until k == 0.
false_positives.suggestion: Restore the original loop: for i in range(m - 1, -1, -1): if k == 0: break; k -= 1

The old `drop_or_convert` helper added `self._variables[k].to_base_variable()` for every removed index coordinate; the new code only updates `variables` with `new_variables`, leaving the original `IndexVariable`/`PandasMultiIndexingAdapter`-backed variables in the result after their index entries have been removed.

false_positives.issue: The MultiIndex special case is now gated on `name not in self.dims` instead of the old `index.dim not in dims_or_levels`. When the MultiIndex dimension and one of its levels are reset together (e.g. `reset_index(['x', 'a'])`), the level is still treated as a partial reset and a new index is created for the remaining levels, whereas the old code reset the whole MultiIndex.

When resetting a MultiIndex dimension with drop=True, only `name` is appended to drop_variables; the MultiIndex level coordinates are not dropped, so they remain as coordinates even though their index was removed. The old code added index.dim plus all level names in this branch.

coord_names no longer subtracts drop_variables. When reset_index(..., drop=True) removes a coordinate, its name stays in coord_names even though the variable was removed from variables, leaving coord_names referencing variables that no longer exist.

Using self._replace instead of self._replace_with_new_dims leaves self._dims unchanged. If reset_index drops the last variable(s) using a dimension (e.g. a Dataset with only an indexed coordinate), the returned Dataset still lists that dimension in dims even though no variable references it.

`maybe_drop_indexes += list(current_coord_names) + var_names` assumes `var_names` is a list. But `_var_names` may be a tuple (a `Sequence`), e.g. `set_index(x=('a', 'b'))`, and `list + tuple` raises `TypeError`.

`drop_variables` now always contains the variable name being indexed, and the old `if dim in self._coord_names: drop_variables.remove(dim)` was removed. In the common `set_index(x='x')` case, the new index variable is added to `new_variables`, but the unchanged deletion loop then deletes it because `x` is in `drop_variables`, leaving an index with no coordinate variable.

`coord_names = set(new_variables) | self._coord_names` no longer subtracts `drop_variables`. With `reset_index(..., drop=True)`, dropped coordinate names remain in `_coord_names` even though their variables were deleted, producing an inconsistent Dataset.
